newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 13.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Monday:
- People are asking tough questions about how Nextwave Telecom Inc will pay the $775,000 per day it owes for PCS licences.

- Though Cuba granted CNN permission to begin operations in Havana more than two months ago, the news organization is facing resistence from the American government as it tries to open its Cuban bureau.
- Awash in new, high-paying technology jobs, the Silicon Valley is in the midst of its most remorkable economic boom in two decades.
- Team Rental is expected to announce today that it is acquiring Budget Rent A Car for more than $350 million from Ford.
- Bill Gates will introduce Office '97, the new version of Microsoft's software bundle for office computing.
- Rupert Murdoch's News Corp which has had little success on the Internet, is trying again, this time under the eye of Murdoch's 24-year-old son, James.

- At a time when Apple Computer most needed to send a message of confidence and clarity, its performance at the Macworld exposition in San Francisco offered little evidence that it had begun digging itself out of its hole.
- After Domino's Pizza unexpectedly announuced it would begin a review of its national advertising account, Grey Advertising in New York declined to participate.
- A book written by Toshihide Iguchi, the Daiwa Bank trader who lost $1.1 billion in the bond market over a dozen years, is gathering attention in Tokyo's publishing world.
- Privacy and anonymity are rarely guaranteed on the Internet, but help may be available.
- The legal battle between H.J. Heinz Co and Campbell Soup over Heinz's attempt to hire away a Campbell executive is headed for mediation.
